Lett. | former_name = Soviet Technical Physics Letters (1975—1993) | publisher = [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]], Pleiades Publishing | country = | frequency = Monthly | history = 1975—present | openaccess = | license = | impact = 0.9 | impact-year = 2024 | website = https://link.springer.com/journal/11455 | link1 = https://link.springer.com/journal/11455 | link1-name = Online access | link2 = https://link.springer.com/journal/11455/volumes-and-issues | link2-name = Online archive | JSTOR = | OCLC = | LCCN = | CODEN = TPLEED | ISSN = 1063-7850 | eISSN = 1090-6533 }} '''''Technical Physics Letters''''' is a [[peer-reviewed]] [[scientific journal]] co-published monthly by [[Springer Science+Business Media]] and Pleiades Publishing. {{Short description|Controversies around the Nobel Prize in Physics}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=November 2020}}
{{Infobox award
| name = Nobel Prize in Physics
| image = Nobel Prize.png
| alt = A golden medallion with an embossed image of a bearded man facing left in profile. To the left of the man is the text "ALFR•" then "NOBEL", and on the right, the text (smaller) "NAT•" then "MDCCCXXXIII" above, followed by (smaller) "OB•" then "MDCCCXCVI" below.
| awarded_for = Outstanding contributions to mankind in the field of physics
| presenter = {{ubl|[[Swedish Academy]]|[[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]]|[[Karolinska Institutet]]|[[Norwegian Nobel Committee]]}}
| country = {{ubl|[[Sweden]]|[[Norway]]}}
| year = {{start date and age|df=yes|1901}}
| most_awards = [[John Bardeen]] (2)
| website = {{URL|https://www.nobelprize.org/physics/}}
}}

Since the [[1901 Nobel Prize in Physics|first award in 1901]], conferment of the [[Nobel Prize]]s, including the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]], has engendered [[Nobel Prize controversies|criticism and controversies]].<ref name="NobelC">[https://physicsworld.com/a/nobel-population-1901-50-anatomy-of-a-scientific-elite/ Nobel population 1901–50: anatomy of a scientific elite]. 5 November 2001. physicsworld.com. Retrieved 20 March 2011.</ref><ref>"[http://news.independent.co.uk/europe/article319509.ece A Nobel calling: 100 years of controversy] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071224170132/http://news.independent.co.uk/europe/article319509.ece |date=24 December 2007 }}", The Independent, 14 October 2005.</ref> After his death in 1896, the will of Swedish industrialist [[Alfred Nobel]] established that an annual prize be awarded for service to humanity in the fields of [[Nobel Prize in Physics|physics]], [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry|chemistry]], [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine|physiology or medicine]], [[Nobel Prize in Literature|literature]], and [[Nobel Peace Prize|peace]]. Similarly, the [[Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel]], first awarded in 1969, is awarded along with the Nobel Prizes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Winners of the Nobel Prize for Economics {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Winners-of-the-Nobel-Prize-for-Economics-1856936 |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=www.britannica.com |language=en}}</ref>

Nobel sought to reward "those who, during the preceding year, shall have conferred the greatest benefit on mankind". One prize, he stated, should be given "to the person who shall have made the most important 'discovery' or 'invention' within the field of physics". Awards committees have historically rewarded discoveries over inventions: {{Asof|2004|lc=y}}, 77 percent of [[Nobel Prize in Physics|Nobel Prizes in Physics]] had given to discoveries, compared with only 23 percent to inventions.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Christoph Bartneck  |author2=Matthias Rauterberg |name-list-style=amp |title=Physics Nobels should favour inventions|journal=Nature|volume=448|page=644|year=2007|doi=10.1038/448644c|issue=7154|pmid=17687300|bibcode = 2007Natur.448..644B|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1386/tear.6.1.73/1|url=http://www.bartneck.de/publications/2008/nobel/bartneckTechnoeticArts2008.pdf|journal=Technoetic Arts: A Journal of Speculative Research|volume=6|issue=1|year=2008|title=The asymmetry between discoveries and inventions in the Nobel Prize in Physics|author1=Christoph Bartneck |author2=Matthias Rauterberg |name-list-style=amp}}</ref>

A major controversy-generating factor for the more recent physics-related prizes is the Nobel rule that each award can not be shared by more than two different research areas and no more than three different individuals each year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Statutes of the Nobel Foundation |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/about/statutes-of-the-nobel-foundation/ |access-date=2022-12-07 |website=NobelPrize.org |date=9 August 2018 |language=en-US}}</ref> This rule was adequate in 1901, when most of the science research was performed by individual scientists working with their small group of assistants in relative isolation. But in more recent times science research has increasingly become a matter of widespread international cooperation and exchange of ideas among different research groups.  These groups are themselves composed of dozens or even hundreds of researchers - modern science has been described as "the teamiest of team sports".<ref>{{cite web |title=Do we need the Nobels?|url=https://www.statnews.com/2016/10/07/nobel-prize-science/}}</ref> The three-person limit has led to glaring omissions<ref>{{cite journal |doi = 10.1038/scientificamerican1012-12|title = Solve the Nobel Prize Dilemma|journal = Scientific American|volume = 307|issue = 4|page = 12|year = 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/nobels-three-winner-limit-does-not-reflect-modern-science/ |title=Nobel's three-winner limit does not reflect modern science}}</ref> of key participants in awarded research.  As an example, the 2017 prize awarded for [[gravitational waves]] could not acknowledge the work of the huge [[LIGO]] consortium.  Similarly, the 2013 prize for [[Search for the Higgs boson|discovery of the Higgs boson]] did not reward the discovering [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS]]/[[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS]] collaboration at [[CERN]].  The latter collaboration included a list of researchers filling 15 single-spaced pages.<ref>{{cite journal
 | collaboration = ATLAS Collaboration, CMS Collaboration
 | title = Combined Measurement of the Higgs Boson Mass in pp Collisions at √s=7 and 8 TeV with the ATLAS and CMS Experiments
 | journal = [[Physical Review Letters]]
 | volume = 114
 | issue = 19
 | article-number = 191803
 | date = 2015-05-14
 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.114.191803
 | url = https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.114.191803
 | publisher = American Physical Society
| hdl = 10400.26/26810
 | hdl-access = free
 | arxiv = 1503.07589
 }}</ref>

The two area, three person limit, with no prizes to organizations, is not mentioned in Nobel's will, but was added by the award committee.  The [[Nobel Peace Prize]], for example, has long been granted to organizations as well as individuals.  This would certainly have been appropriate in physics for cases such as ATLAS/CMS or [[LIGO]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.theatlantic.com/science/archive/2017/10/the-absurdity-of-the-nobel-prizes-in-science/541863/ |title = The Absurdity of the Nobel Prizes in Science|website = [[The Atlantic]]|date = 3 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2018/sep/30/nobel-prize-fails-modern-science |title = Why Nobel prizes fail 21st-century science|newspaper = The Guardian|date = 30 September 2018}}</ref>

'''Carceral geography''' is a field of [[human geography]] that explores “[[Carceral archipelago|carceral spaces]]”, which include prisons, concentration camps, immigration detention centers, [[black site]]s, and other spaces where people are confined. Carceral geographers may study the [[Prison design|design of prison spaces]] and how these spaces are experienced by imprisoned people and surrounding communities. They also study changes in carceral spaces over time, intersecting with [[historical geography]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |title=Historical geographies of prisons: unlocking the usable carceral past |date=2015 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-317-53262-0 |editor-last=Morin |editor-first=Karen M. |series=Routledge research in historical geography |location=London}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Citation |last=Schliehe |first=Anna |chapter=Contextualising Carceral Geography and Youth Justice: What About Young Women? |date=2021-08-11 |title=Young Women's Carceral Geographies: Abandonment, Trouble and Mobility |pages=15–37 |chapter-url=http://www.emerald.com/books/monograph/12491/chapter/82691568 |access-date=2025-10-22 |publisher=Emerald Publishing Limited |doi=10.1108/978-1-83909-049-320211002 |isbn=978-1-83909-050-9|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Morin |first=Karen |date=2013 |title=DISTINGUISHED HISTORICAL GEOGRAPHY LECTURE, 2013 Carceral Space and the Usable Past |url=https://bucknell.elsevierpure.com/ws/portalfiles/portal/39748615/fulltext.pdf |journal=Historical Geography |volume=41 |pages=1–21}}</ref>

Geographers give attention to the politics and placement of prison facilities, and how carceral practices are shaped by [[settler colonialism]] and [[racial capitalism]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last=Bloch |first=Stefano |date=Jul 2024 |title=A Legal Geography of Prison and Other Carceral Spaces |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/anti.13028 |journal=Antipode |language=en |volume=56 |issue=4 |pages=1152–1171 |doi=10.1111/anti.13028 |issn=0066-4812|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

'''Exail Technologies''' (written as '''EXAIL''') is a French technology company based in [[La Garde, Var|La Garde]] ([[Var (department)|Département Var]]). The group was formed in 2022 from the merger of drone and robotics specialist ECA Group and navigation and photonics provider iXblue. Exail develops unmanned systems, inertial and navigation sensors, and optical components for civil and military applications and is represented in around 80 countries. In 2024, the family-run company generated sales of around €373 million with approximately 2,000 employees. According to the company, Exail generates around 56 percent of its sales in the defense sector, while 44 percent comes from civilian applications.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|access-date=2025-10-09 |language=en-US |title=The Group in brief |url=https://www.exail-technologies.com/overview/ |website=Exail Technologies}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> The group is listed on the [[Euronext Paris|Paris Stock Exchange]], has been a member of the [[SBF 120]] index since 2025, and is part of the “[[Euronext]] Tech Leaders” segment.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2025-10-09 |author=Actusnews Wire |language=en |title=EXAIL TECHNOLOGIES (ex GROUPE GORGE) |url=https://www.actusnews.com/en/exail-technologies/pr/2025/09/23/exail-technologies-s_a_-launches-an-offering-of-undated-bonds-convertible-into-new-shares-and-or-exchangeable-for-existing}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

[[File:Regeneração em Hydra.png|thumb|Regeneration in [[Hydra (genus)|Hydra]].]]

'''Regenerative biology''' is a branch of [[biology]] that studies the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which organisms replace or reconstitute cells, tissues, or body parts lost due to injury or cell death. This article focuses on the biological aspects: cellular principles, signaling pathways, animal models, and evolutionary hypotheses explaining the differences between highly regenerative organisms and those with limited regenerative capacity.<ref name="vila-farre" />

'''''Music, Fashion, Film''''' is the eighth studio album<ref>{{cite news|first=Lindsay|last=Zoladz|date=24 July 2026|title=Charli XCX Makes a Quick and Dirty Exit From Her ''Brat'' Era|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/24/arts/music/charli-xcx-music-fashion-film.html|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=27 July 2026|quote=''Music, Fashion, Film'', the ... eighth album by Charli XCX}}</ref> by the British singer-songwriter [[Charli XCX]], released on 24 July 2026 and distributed through [[Atlantic Records]]. A [[Pop music|pop]] album, it features production by her longtime collaborators [[A. G. Cook]] and [[Finn Keane]], who both co-wrote the album with Charli.

The album was preceded by the release of four singles, all of which have accompanying music videos; the lead single "[[Rock Music (song)|Rock Music]]", followed by "[[SS26 (song)|SS26]]", "[[Wink Wink]]" and "[[Camera (Charli XCX song)|Camera]]". A film of the same name accompanies the album, which includes visuals for all 11 songs, as well as behind-the-scenes footage of the album's creation.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Pilley |first=Max |url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/watch-charli-xcxs-full-music-fashion-film-album-film-3958934 |title=Watch Charli XCX’s full ''Music, Fashion, Film'' album film |magazine=[[NME]] |date=25 July 2026 |access-date=1 August 2026 |archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2026-0801-1000-54/https://www.nme.com:443/news/music/watch-charli-xcxs-full-music-fashion-film-album-film-3958934 |archive-date=1 August 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Upon release, ''Music, Fashion, Film'' received acclaim from [[Music journalism|music critics]], who praised its lyrical honesty and experimental production. It topped the charts in Australia, Belgium (Flanders), Hungary, New Zealand, Scotland, and the United Kingdom, while reaching the top ten in multiple countries including Austria, Germany, Ireland, Finland, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United States. To further promote the album, Charli embarked on the [[Music, Fashion, Film Tour|eponymous fifth concert tour]] from September 2026 to February 2027.

'''The Brick''' is a visual art space in [[Los Angeles, California]]. 

It was founded as '''LAXART''' in 2005 by Lauri Firstenberg. In 2015, The Brick moved into a former 1928 recording studio<ref name="about">{{cite web |title=About |url=https://the-brick.org/about |website=The Brick |access-date=11 May 2026}}</ref>. It moved again and until 2022 was in [[West Hollywood]] in a space now occupied by famed curator and former [[MOCA LA]] director [[Jeffrey Dietch]]'s gallery.<ref name="newbldg" /> The latest space opened on June 16, 2024.<ref name="newbldg">{{cite news |last1=Finkel |first1=Jori |title=Los Angeles non-profit LAXART prepares to re-open in new home with new name |url=https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2024/05/22/laxart-the-brick-new-location-name |access-date=11 May 2026 |publisher=The Art Newspaper |date=May 22, 2024}}</ref>

The name was inspired by the exposed brick walls of the new location, the idea the space is part of a cooperative community with a construction role, and also the notion of a brick as a tool or weapon or revolution.<ref name="newbldg" />

The Brick has 4,000 square feet (370 square meters) of exhibition space, plus a courtyard.<ref name="newbldg" />

[[Hamza Walker]] became the director in 2016.

'''Fidelity''', in [[molecular biology]], refers to the accuracy of [[Central dogma of molecular biology|replication]] of genetic material, such as DNA or RNA. Replication errors result in mutations that can negatively affect cell viability and health, however, can provide genetic variation to a population.

'''Animato''', sometimes given as '''anima''', '''animando''', or '''animandosi''',<ref name="Harvard">{{cite book|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Harvard_Dictionary_of_Music/02rFSecPhEsC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22animato%22+%22Harvard%22&pg=PA46&printsec=frontcover|title=The Harvard Dictionary of Music, Fourth Edition|chapter=Animando, animandosi, animanto|editor-first= Don Michael|editor-last= Randel|publisher=[[Harvard University Press]]|page=46}}</ref> or in its French form '''animé''', is a lesser-known [[musical expression]] and [[tempo marking]] that was used in [[Western classical music]] during the 18th and 19th centuries.<ref name="Grove">{{Cite encyclopedia|date=2001|first1=David |last1= Fallows  | entry=Animato (It.: ‘lively’, ‘enlivened’; past participle of animare, ‘to enliven’)|encyclopedia=[[Grove Music Online]]|publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |doi=10.1093/gmo/9781561592630.article.00953}}{{subscription required}}</ref> The word animato is taken from the past participle form of the Italian word animare, meaning "to enliven".<ref>{{cite book|chapter=Glossary of music terms|title=100 Piano Classics to Grow On|year=2004|publisher=Ekay Music|editor-first=Edward J.|editor-last= Shanaphy|page=XV|isbn= 9781929009169}}</ref> ''[[The Harvard Dictionary of Music]]'' defines the term as meaning "Animating, becoming animated, animated; usually with the implication of (increasingly) rapid tempo."<ref name="Harvard"/> However, ''[[Grove Music Online]]'' states that the term was interpreted to mean varying things with French theorist [[Sébastien de Brossard]] defining the term as synonymous with the tempo marking [[allegro (music)|allegro]] in 1703. According to musicologist [[David Fallows]], the tradition of increasing spreed in connection with the animato tempo marking was not firmly established until the 19th century.<ref name="Grove"/>

While a lesser used marking, some well known compositions the contain the animato marking include Leonara's act 1 cavatina from Verdi's ''[[Il trovatore]]'' (1853), the Dies irae from Verdi's ''[[Messa da Requiem]]'' (1874), and the second movement of [[Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky]]'s [[Symphony No. 5 (Tchaikovsky)|Symphony No. 5]] (1888).<ref name="Grove"/>

'''Testimonial literature''' is [[autobiography|autobiographical]] writing specific to the author that presents a real-life account of trauma, oppression, or survival to bear witness to [[social injustice]].<ref name="Donovan2016">{{cite book |last1=Donovan |first1=Sarah |title=Genocide Literature in Middle and Secondary Classrooms: Rhetoric, Witnessing, and Social Action in a Time of Standards and Accountability |date=12 August 2016 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-317-22005-3 |page=42 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Genocide_Literature_in_Middle_and_Second/OU7UDAAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Testimonial+literature&pg=PT42 |access-date=4 September 2026 |language=en}}</ref> It is a 
[[Genre#subgenre|subgenre]] of [[Psychological trauma|trauma]] literature<ref name="Nguyet2026">{{cite book |last1=Nguyet |first1=Nguyen Thi |title=Shadows of Silence: English–Finnish Parallel Tales |date=25 May 2026 |publisher=Nguyen Thi Nguyet |page=69 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/SHADOWS_OF_SILENCE_English_Finnish_Paral/UcbcEQAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Testimonial+literature&pg=PT69 |access-date=4 September 2026 |language=en}}</ref> and the [[non-fiction novel]]. While it can be traced to 1970s and 1980s civil conflicts in [[Latin America]],<ref name="ChingBuckleyLozano2009" /> accounts of historical, political, and social incidents of the twentieth century, such as [[World War I]] and [[World War II]], have also been written in this format,<ref name="KimKangGroskyArslanPissinou2012">{{cite book |last1=Kim |first1=Tai-hoon |last2=Kang |first2=Jeong Jin |last3=Grosky |first3=William I. |last4=Arslan |first4=Tughrul |last5=Pissinou |first5=Niki |title=Computer Applications for Bio-technology, Multimedia and Ubiquitous City: International Conferences, MulGraB, BSBT and IUrC 2012, Held as Part of the Future Generation Information Technology Conference, FGIT 2012, Gangneug, Korea, December 16-19, 2012. Proceedings |date=28 November 2012 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-642-35521-9 |pages=246-47 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Computer_Applications_for_Bio_technology/c425BQAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Testimonial+literature&pg=PA246 |access-date=4 September 2026 |language=en}}</ref> as was Dr. L. T. Leach's "cancer cure" of 1903.<ref name="Cancer1922">{{cite book |author1=Propaganda Department of the Journal of the American Medical Association |title=Cancer "cures" and "treatments" |date=1922 |publisher=The Department |location=Chicago |page=37 |edition=Public domain |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Cancer_cures_and_treatments/vhUyAQAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Testimonial+literature&pg=PA37 |access-date=4 September 2026 |language=en}}</ref> With a dependence on its readers,<ref name="HeidenMarinescu2025">{{cite book |editor1-last=Heiden |editor1-first=Gert-Jan van der |editor2-last=Marinescu |editor2-first=Paul |title=The Phenomenology of Testimony: From Inner Truth to Shared World |date=10 March 2025 |publisher=BRILL |isbn=978-90-04-72707-6 |page=179 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Phenomenology_of_Testimony/j91MEQAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Testimonial+literature&pg=PA179 |access-date=4 September 2026 |language=en}}</ref> the genre includes transcribing, editing, and marketing for impact.<ref name="ChingBuckleyLozano2009">{{cite book |last1=Ching |first1=Erik |last2=Buckley |first2=Christina |last3=Lozano-Alonso |first3=Angélica |title=Reframing Latin America: A Cultural Theory Reading of the Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries |date=3 June 2009 |publisher=University of Texas Press |isbn=978-0-292-78265-5 |page=318 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Reframing_Latin_America/Rtyujouz6FUC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Testimonial+literature&pg=PA318 |access-date=4 September 2026 |language=en}}</ref> Works of this genre face questions of authenticity.<ref name="SmithWatson1998">{{cite book |last1=Smith |first1=Sidonie |last2=Watson |first2=Julia |title=Women, Autobiography, Theory: A Reader |date=1998 |publisher=Univ of Wisconsin Press |isbn=978-0-299-15844-6 |page=210 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Women_Autobiography_Theory/cxiULJrkytIC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Testimonial+literature&pg=PA210 |access-date=4 September 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

Some published [[oral history|oral]] or written [[autobiography|autobiographical]] [[narrative]]s are considered "testimonial literature", particularly when they present [[evidence (law)|evidence]] or [[first-person narrative|first person]] accounts of [[human rights]] abuses, [[violence]] and [[war]], and living under conditions of social [[oppression]]. This usage of the term comes originally from [[Latin America]] and the Spanish term ''"[[testimonio]]"'' when it emerged from human rights [[tribunal]]s, [[truth commissions]], and other [[international human rights instruments]] in countries such as [[Chile]] and [[Argentina]]. One of the most famous, though controversial, of these works to be translated into English is ''[[I, Rigoberta Menchú]]''. The autobiographies of [[Frederick Douglass]] can be considered among the earliest significant English-language works in this [[genre]]. The biographies of marginalized women such as [[Jesusita Aragón|Jesusita Aragon]] and [[Maria Elena Lucas]], made from recordings and transcriptions by oral historian [[Fran Leeper Buss]], are more recent examples.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Books and Works By Author Fran Leeper Buss |url=https://www.franleeperbuss.com/authored-books-and-works |access-date=2024-04-20 |website=Franleeperbuss |language=en}}</ref>

'''Wood biology''' is a sub-area of [[wood science]], which is related to the biological formation, development, structure, composition, and function of [[wood]] ([[xylem]]) and its constituent tissues.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Groover | first1=Andrew | last2=Mansfield | first2=Shawn D. | title=An introduction to a Virtual Issue on Wood Biology | journal=New Phytologist | volume=225 | issue=4 | date=2020 | issn=0028-646X | doi=10.1111/nph.16384 | pages=1401–1403 | url=https://nph.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/nph.16384 | access-date=2026-09-14}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title= A brief overview on the development of wood research| website=De Gruyter Brill | url=https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/hf-2021-0155/html | access-date=2026-09-14}} 3. Wood biology (pg. 109)</ref> It examines wood at [[macroscopic]], [[microscopic]], and [[molecular]] levels, linking the biology of [[tree]]s and woody plants with the structure and properties of their [[xylem]] (wood).<ref>{{cite book
|last1=Schmitt |first1=Uwe
|last2=Koch |first2=Gerald
|last3=Hietz |first3=Peter
|last4=Tholen |first4=Daniel
|title=Springer Handbook of Wood Science and Technology
|chapter=Wood Biology
|publisher=Springer International Publishing
|publication-place=Cham
|year=2023
|pages=41–138
|doi=10.1007/978-3-030-81315-4_3
}}</ref>

It includes the study of [[wood anatomy]], [[xylem]] formation, cell types and tissues, and the biological processes responsible for the growth of wood. It also studies the variations in wood structure among [[tree]] species, within individual woody trees, and in response to environmental and other parameters.
